human_tolerance.notes: Authored conservative defaults; ADW reports use of freshwater wetlands and occasional park or golf-course ponds.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Mating season is reported in May and June. The broad US region includes resident and migratory populations; migration timing varies by population and is not encoded as a national calendar.

taxonomy.note: Both providers return accepted Fulica americana at species rank; GBIF exact ACCEPTED match (usage key 2474393), iNaturalist active species taxon 473.

external.note: Identifiers resolved independently at their respective providers on 2026-11-01.

range.note: Distribution and habitat describes the species across North America and year-round and breeding occupancy in the United States; US is the only supported region in this record.

traits.limb_count.note: Standard avian anatomy: two legs; wings are not legs. GBIF backbone independently resolves the taxon to Aves.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Physical Description and Behavior: walks on land, swims with lobed toes, and flies.

traits.respiration.note: Authored standard avian anatomy; ADW classifies it as Aves.

traits.nest_type.note: Reproduction section: nest built at reed edge with ramp to water.

traits.perching.note: No perching behavior is described; false is an authored default for this aquatic rail.

traits.size_class.note: Small is consistent with 0.4508 kg average mass.

traits.mass_kg.note: Authored representative mass: midpoint of the midpoints of the sex-specific ranges in Description (female 427-628 g; male 576-848 g), rounded to 0.62 kg. This is a modelling estimate, not a published sex-combined mean.

traits.length_m.note: Description gives 34-43 cm; midpoint 38.5 cm converted to metres.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Description gives 58-71 cm; midpoint 64.5 cm converted to metres.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Animal Diversity Web Lifespan/Longevity lines 125-135: “average lifespan” 9.0 years, status wild. The adjacent 268 months value is explicitly linked to the Bird Banding Laboratory and is a maximum-age record; it was excluded. The old ADW page cites Grzimek (1975) and Terres (1980) for its average statement but gives no estimator or study population.

traits.diet.note: Authored simulation allocations, not measured dietary proportions: ADW Food Habits lists pond vegetation, insects, fish/tadpoles and other small aquatic animals; the weights divide feeding actions for this model. The schema distinguishes fish and other vertebrate shares.

traits.social.note: Flock based on regularly found in sizable flocks; group size interval is an authored simulation range.

traits.defense.note: Flee is an authored main response based on descriptions of escape and aquatic behavior; nest defense is outside this simple response field.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement, authored as moderate wariness for a flocking waterbird that moves away from threats.

habitat.use.note: Judgement: mostly aquatic; smaller ground and aerial shares reflect shoreline foraging and flight.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Water is the primary habitat; authored as shelter proxy.

habitat.resources.note: Feeding lists aquatic vegetation, arthropods, fish and other aquatic animals. Because the resource vocabulary has no fish tag, fish is mapped to small_vertebrate for feeding actions; allocations are authored, not measured.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Urban affinity is authored Adapter based on occurrence at freshwater wetlands and open water; numeric tolerance and garden use values are conservative model choices.

seasonal.strategy.note: The account describes US populations that migrate and others that remain year-round where water stays open; PartialMigration represents that mix without assigning a national fraction.

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding section: mating in May and June. Distribution section reports southbound migration August-December and northbound migration late February-mid-May for temperate populations east of the Rockies; these population-specific migration windows are documented here but not applied to all US populations.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Egg/juvenile/adult stages; juvenile duration is an authored rounded simulation interval, source says flying at 5-6 weeks and independence around 2 months.

look.note: Physical Description: dark grey feathers, white undertail patch, white bill with red swelling. Block proportions and palette are authored approximations.

behavior.note: Authored species-local program: walk along shore, swim-gait feeding, fly from threats, rest at night. The format has no dive action, so underwater feeding is represented only as swim-gait foraging.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Description gives female mass 427-628 g and male mass 576-848 g; combined observed range converted to kg.
